speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative check-up. You mentioned occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty; can you describe exactly where the pain is located and how it feels?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain occurs specifically when you eat and when earrings touch the ear; does this sensation involve a visible ridge or lump in the ear canal that prevents the earring from sitting flush, and have you noticed any discharge or fever? REQUEST TEST: Otoscopy with microscopy.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal neuralgia (Gasserian syndrome). The pain triggered by chewing and the history of prior ear infections are classic signs of nerve entrapment in the parotid region, despite the clear CT scan which rules out recurrent cholesteatoma or bone erosion.
